title: Do simulated readers' scores depend on what the wiki says? Intact against degraded copies of a finished wiki, with a no-wiki baseline

document.name: nlogn
document.title: Integer multiplication below n log n (paper.tex)

task: simulated readers: one round on full-v0.6-latex-planner-handoff (25 pages): 9 goals (34 key points), 18 read and 9 baseline tasks per copy, graded per copy
question: Does reader coverage rise with the wiki (lift over baseline) and fall when the key paragraphs are deleted (sensitivity)?

binary.commit: exegenius 0.6.0 (target/debug/exegenius sha256 c37a2b3d…caee8), not rebuilt during the run

protocol: general-purpose subagents from the development session: readers and baselines on Haiku high, goals and grades on Sonnet high (calibration/plans/SR1.md)
preregistration: calibration/plans/SR1.md (preregistered 17:49 UTC, 2026-10-17, before any SR1 model call)
comparison: intact against degraded (sensitivity) and against the baseline (lift); fixed rows

intended.task_prompt: the read and baseline tasks as rendered by exegenius 0.6.0; grade tasks on claude-sonnet-5-5 high
as intact, on the copy with 31 key paragraphs deleted

primary_preregistered.value: C_int 57/68 = 0.838, C_deg 47/68 = 0.691, C_base 7/68 = 0.103; lift 0.735, sensitivity 0.147 (row 1 needs 0.15). Row 3: inconclusive; propose rounds = 0 by default

exploratory.value: 15 of 18 baseline answers decline by instruction, so lift does not test prior knowledge; sensitivity sits in the held-out goals (12/22 -> 5/22) not the repair goals (45/46 -> 42/46); stuck points occur on the deleted pages as often in the intact copy (18/18 runs; 148 vs 142 stuck points)

cache_read_tokens.value: 37.9 M for 74 subagents (661 calls); ~19 M per round per copy

deviations.what: readers ran as general-purpose subagents (every tool), not exegenius-reader (Read, Write, Bash); some created 6 stray sessions (archived; one ran a turn with no task, ~61 k tokens, outside the spend counts)
the deletion rule was operationalised mechanically (top content-word overlap per key point, plus overlap >= 0.35) before any reader run

limitations: One wiki of an older pipeline, one round, one reader profile, one run per goal and start.
The baseline is an instructed refusal, not a measure of what the reader model knows.
